messages:
sam (support): @irene got your escalation — you said pods in prod are getting NXDOMAIN for the service endpoint after the deploy? can you paste a dig from a failing pod?
irene (customer): yes. from a pod: 
```
$ dig svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal @127.0.0.53
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal @127.0.0.53
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 54321
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal. IN A
```
this happens from all pods in the namespace, but curl to the public API works from outside VPC.
sam (support): thanks. can you also paste the node-local-dns / forwarder logs (if available) and the forwarder's upstream resolvers?
irene (customer): forwarder is at 10.0.2.3 (central-dns). node-local forwards to that. logs show a bunch of queries and NXDOMAIN. nothing obvious.
devon (sre-oncall): quick test — run dig against the central forwarder over UDP and TCP separately: `dig @10.0.2.3 svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal +notcp` and `dig @10.0.2.3 svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal +tcp`
(irene ran tests and pasted outputs):
```
$ dig @10.0.2.3 svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal +notcp
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 11111
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0

$ dig @10.0.2.3 svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal +tcp
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 22222
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1
svc-api.prod.svc.endpoint.company.internal. 60 IN A 10.10.50.12
```
so UDP path is failing/servfail but TCP succeeds and returns the expected A. that smells like truncated UDP answers or firewall blocking TCP fallback.
mike (eng-dns): interesting — Route53 sometimes returns responses that require TCP fallback (big records / DNSSEC / long record sets). If UDP is truncated the client should retry over TCP. If TCP is blocked outbound from the forwarder, the client never gets the full answer. can you check iptables/egress rules on the central forwarder host?
sam (support): @irene any egress allowlist in your infra that might block TCP/53 from the forwarder?
irene (customer): we have a strict egress policy — only UDP/53 allowed to the resolver IPs (10.0.2.3, 10.0.3.3). tcp/53 was intentionally blocked (wasn't aware DNS might need TCP).
devon (sre-oncall): can you run `iptables -L -n | grep "dpt:53"` on the forwarder?
irene (customer): pasted output:
```
Chain OUTPUT (policy ACCEPT)
num  target     prot opt source               destination
1    ACCEPT     udp  --  0.0.0.0/0            10.0.2.3            udp dpt:domain
2    DROP       tcp  --  0.0.0.0/0            10.0.2.3            tcp dpt:domain
```
mike (eng-dns): there it is. TCP to port 53 is dropped to the upstream resolver. when Route53 returns large/complex answers, the resolver will respond with TC flag and the client must retry over TCP to get the full record. because TCP is blocked, the forwarder returns SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN to clients (some resolvers treat truncated responses as NXDOMAIN depending on cache/implementation).
sam (support): short repro steps (for our runbook):
1) from a pod: `dig @127.0.0.53 svc-api...` -> NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL
2) from forwarder host: `dig @10.0.2.3 svc-api... +notcp` -> SERVFAIL
3) from forwarder host: `dig @10.0.2.3 svc-api... +tcp` -> A records
4) `iptables -L -n | grep dpt:53` shows DROP for tcp to 10.0.2.3
root cause: egress policy blocking TCP/53 from central forwarder -> prevents TCP fallback for truncated DNS responses -> forwarder returns failure to node-local resolvers -> pods see NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL for service endpoint.
devon (sre-oncall): mitigation options: allow tcp/53 to the resolver IPs from forwarder OR enable EDNS size reduction / split answers (not reliable). recommend updating egress allowlist to permit TCP/53.
irene (customer): I'm opening a ticket with infra to add the rule now. ETA 30m. any quick temp workaround?
mike (eng-dns): temporary: reduce the RRset size by removing extra records or shorten TXT records if any, but that's not always possible. Best temporary fix is to allow TCP/53.
dns-bot: incident-note: root_cause=egress_block_tcp53; affected=pods-in-namespace; severity=low-medium; action=egress-rule-update
sam (support): once infra confirms rule change, try `kubectl exec` into a pod and run `dig` again and paste results. please cc this thread.
irene (customer): infra updated rule -> TCP/53 allowed. retested, dig from pod now returns the A and curl to internal endpoint works.
sam (support): great — marking resolved. root cause summary: central forwarder had TCP/53 blocked by egress allowlist which prevented TCP fallback for truncated/large Route53 responses causing NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL at node-local and pod level. fix: allow TCP/53 to upstream resolvers. :white_check_mark:
devon (sre-oncall): adding a short KB note to support runbook about ensuring both UDP and TCP 53 are allowed for forwarders and node-local caches.
